section_summary: This section contains the concluding portion of an operational history of Operation Iceberg and the Battle of Okinawa, followed by the first five chapters of an extensive civil affairs handbook titled 'Okinawa Background Information'. The military narrative describes the tactical phases of the 1945 Okinawa campaign, the death of Tenth Army commander General Simon Bolivar Buckner Jr., General Joseph Stilwell's assumption of command, and the final Japanese surrender ceremony in September 1945. The background handbook, compiled by the U.S. Naval Military Government Education Department, provides a comprehensive overview of Ryukyuan geography, natural resources, dynastic history, culture, religion, burial traditions, and prewar Japanese prefectural government, police administration, and economic conditions.

subfiles.about: A narrative account of Operation Iceberg, the Battle of Okinawa, and the surrender of Japanese forces in the Ryukyu Islands.
subfiles.summary: Details the amphibious landings, fierce fighting along the Machinato and Shuri lines, the capture of Ie Shima, General Buckner's death, General Stilwell assuming command, and the formal Ryukyu surrender at Tenth Army Headquarters.
subfiles.title: Operation "Iceberg" and the Battle of Okinawa

subfiles.about: A comprehensive military government handbook surveying the geography, history, society, religion, customs, government, and economy of Okinawa and the Ryukyu Islands.
subfiles.from: U.S. Naval Military Government Headquarters Education Department
subfiles.summary: Compiled by the U.S. Naval Military Government Education Department, this handbook presents detailed background intelligence on Okinawa and the Ryukyus for occupation personnel. It covers physical geography, weather, flora and fauna, and traces Okinawan history from mythological origin traditions through the unified kingdom, Chinese tributary relations, Satsuma dominion, and modern Japanese annexation. Later chapters analyze population demographics, social customs, indigenous religion and Christianity, ancestral turtle-back tomb burial rituals, and the prewar Japanese system of local government, police authority, public health, education, and economy.
subfiles.title: Okinawa Background Information
